guidance_policy.purpose: Reference knowledge for architecture, utilities, and workflows
usage: Use this file for context and examples
When guidance conflicts with rules or repo reality, follow rules and current code
For ports, scripts, and route topology, verify package.json, server/config.js, server/routes/*, and webpack.config*.js
Default, mock, or sample hardcoded data → data/ only (see data_folder); helpers/ is mapping/transform logic only

data_folder.purpose: Canonical home for hardcoded seed data: example structures, defaults, and mock values used as samples or local fallbacks before/atop CMS.
agent_rules: When you need default, mock, fixture, or sample data to illustrate shape or fill dev/demo — add or extend files under data/, not helpers/, route config modules in server/controllers/, or inline in routes.
helpers/ holds mapping and transform logic (geo, article, property, url, path); data/ holds the actual payload objects and CSV sources.
Page/comp/theme samples sync to CMS via cms/scripts/seed-and-sync.js; prefer CMS API for production updates (see cms/API.md).

layout.index.js: Geo CSV ingest (data/csv → dist JSON), getGeoData() cache — runtime reference data, not page content
layout.page/: Page section arrays + layout (hero, points, gallery, …); one file per page key (e.g. index.js, ai-trend.js); see data/page/README.md
layout.comps/: Reusable comp seed objects (header, footer, theme-*, comp_template)
layout.mock/: Mock API/list payloads (e.g. mock/articles.js for property/article cards)
layout.csv/: Source CSV for geo generation (usstates, uscities, uscounties, usneighborhoods, uszips)

examples.new_page_sections: data/page/<page-key>.js — default export ordered section array
examples.new_theme_comp: data/comps/theme-<name>.js — default + dark CSS vars; comp key theme-<name>
examples.new_mock_listing: data/mock/<name>.js — structured sample records matching API/article shape

Emits event if name is string and no function exists

For new code, prefer explicit error behavior based on call-site needs
Log all errors through sendError system
Categorize errors by type (NETWORK, TIMEOUT, HTTP, PARSE, VALIDATION)
Include detailed error information in logs

validation: Validate request data can be stringified

overview: Use defBool and defEnum from client/js/core/def.js to model UI state via CSS class names
Each status is driven by a CSS class on an element and a set of generated methods on exportObj
Prefer these helpers over hand-written add/remove/toggle for consistent behavior

boolean_status.status_property: camelCase version of name on exportObj (e.g. 'headerClose')
methods: add<Status>() – add the class and mark status true (e.g. addHeaderClose)
remove<Status>() – remove the class and mark status false (e.g. removeHeaderClose)
is<Status>() – read-only check of the current DOM/class state (e.g. isHeaderClose)

enum_status.status_property: camelCase version of key on exportObj (e.g. 'view')
methods: switchTo<Value>() – switch to one value and update classes (e.g. switchToGrid)
current<Key>() – read the current enum value (e.g. currentView)

plugin_pattern: Define arrays like boolStatus and enumStatus inside a plugin/page (see client/js/plugins/_header.js and client/pages/demo/index.js)
In init($el, opt, exportObj), loop through boolStatus and enumStatus and call defBool/defEnum to attach all status methods
After init, use the generated methods on exportObj inside the plugin and in templates

import_management.rule: Before adding any import, verify that the function/class is not already defined locally in the file
checklist: Read the entire file or at least function definitions before adding imports
examples: data/index.js: csvToJson and saveAsJson are local functions, not external imports
Always verify local scope before importing from external modules

analysis.enforceTypeScript: preferred for new or heavily modified modules where practical

error_handling.design: Intentional design choice to prevent app crashes
error_handling.impact: All errors are logged but not propagated
error_handling.benefit: Graceful degradation and consistent error handling

response_handling.impact: All HTTP errors are logged but not thrown
response_handling.benefit: Consistent error handling across the application

content_type.design: Falls back to text for non-JSON responses
content_type.impact: May need to handle different response types

url.fix: Use URL constructor or more comprehensive validation

features: Asset management (fonts, images, SCSS, JS, HTML)

environment_configs.stage: webpack.config.build.js with NODE_ENV=stage (.env.stage, CDN for GitHub Pages)

features: devMiddleware.writeToDisk so Node can read built assets from dist/
proxy non-asset requests to app server (APP_HOST, default http://localhost:3000)
CDN public path for GitHub Pages

deploy-gh.process: Publishes dist/ to gh-pages branch (run after build:stage)

development: Webpack dev server with hot reloading

environment_variables.production: .env.production (CDN_HOST empty for AWS same-origin or set AWS/CloudFront URL)

flow: Development: npm run dev → webpack dev server (default :3001) + Node (:3000), proxy between them; hot reload
Local build: npm run build:dev → .env, dist/ output
Stage (GitHub): npm run build:stage → .env.stage → then npm run deploy-gh
Production (AWS): npm run build:prod or npm run build-docker:prod → .env.production
Deploy stage: npm run deploy-gh → publishes dist/ to gh-pages (workflow runs build:stage then deploy-gh on merge to main)

common_issues: Port conflicts: Node PORT (default 3000), webpack dev server WEBPACK_DEV_SERVER_PORT (default 3001), Docker host DOCKER_PORT (default 3002)
